{{Short description|Adjusting test scores based on the test-taker's ethnicity}}
'''Race-norming''', more formally called '''within-group score conversion''' and '''score adjustment strategy''', is the practice of adjusting test scores to account for the race or ethnicity of the test-taker.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Foundations of Psychological Testing: A Practical Approach, Third Edition|last1=Miller|first1=Leslie A.|last2=McIntire|first2=Sandra A.|last3=Lovler|first3=Robert L.|date=2011|publisher=SAGE Publications|isbn=978-1-4129-7639-8|location=Los Angeles, CA|page=50}}</ref> In the United States, it was first implemented by the Federal Government in 1981 with little publicity,<ref>{{Cite book |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=51RmStBo6roC |title=Handbook of Public Personnel Administration |last=Rabin |first=Jack |publisher=[[CRC Press]] |year=1994 |chapter=Race Norming, Validity Generalization, and Employment Testing|page=451|isbn=978-0-8247-9231-2 }}</ref> and was subsequently outlawed by the [[Civil Rights Act of 1991]].<ref name=ppm>{{cite journal|last1=Greenlaw|first1=Paul S.|last2=Jensen|first2=Sanne S.|title=Race-Norming and the Civil Rights Act of 1991|journal=[[Public Personnel Management]]|date=March 1996|volume=25|issue=1|pages=13–24|doi=10.1177/009102609602500102|s2cid=143168254}}</ref> 

Prior to being banned by the federal government, race-norming was practiced by 38 U.S. states' employment services.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YdEiUjrLeiYC&pg=PT68 |title=Foundations of Psychological Testing: A Practical Approach |last1=Miller |first1=Leslie |last2=McIntire |first2=Sandra |last3=Lovler |first3=Robert |publisher=SAGE |year=2011 |page=50|isbn=978-1-4129-7639-8 }}</ref> The aim of this practice is to counteract alleged racial bias in [[aptitude test]]s administered to job applicants,<ref name="ppm" /> as well as in [[neuropsychological test]]s.<ref name="Gasquoine2009">{{cite journal|last1=Gasquoine|first1=Philip G.|title=Race-Norming of Neuropsychological Tests|journal=[[Neuropsychology Review]]|date=19 March 2009|volume=19|issue=2|pages=250–262|doi=10.1007/s11065-009-9090-5|pmid=19294515|s2cid=13933700}}</ref> The argument was that it guarantees racial balance. The practice converted and compared the raw score of the test according to racial groups. The score of a black candidate is only compared to the scores of those who had the same ethnicity. If the candidate's score, which is reported within a percentile range, fell within a certain percentile when compared to white or all candidates, it would be much higher among other black candidates.<ref>{{Cite book|title=When Race Counts: The Morality of Racial Preference in Britain and America|last=Edwards|first=John|date=2005-06-29|publisher=Routledge|isbn=0-415-07292-1|location=New York|pages=[https://archive.org/details/whenracecountsmo0000edwa/page/117 117]|url=https://archive.org/details/whenracecountsmo0000edwa/page/117}}</ref>

==Criticism==

Race-norming has been criticized as racist towards black people and has been compared to [[eugenics]] and [[pseudoscience|pseudoscientific racism]].<ref name="Hobson2021">{{cite news |last1=Hobson |first1=Will |title=How 'race-norming' was built into the NFL concussion settlement |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/08/02/race-norming-nfl-concussion-settlement/ |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=2 August 2021 |access-date=21 October 2021 |quote=Revelations about race-norming have drawn fierce blowback from players and advocates, some of whom have made comparisons to eugenics and other racist pseudoscience and social science leveraged against minority groups throughout history.}}</ref> In 2021, such criticisms surfaced following an announcement by the [[National Football League]] that they will cease to use the practice in determining settlements for players' injuries.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dale |first1=Maryclaire |title=NFL, players agree to end 'race-norming' in $1B settlement |url=https://apnews.com/article/nfl-sports-football-health-philadelphia-f9c8c931467c815099dce0ed42652379 |website=The Associated Press |date=21 October 2021 |access-date=21 October 2021 |quote=The NFL and lawyers for thousands of retired NFL players have reached an agreement to end race-based adjustments in dementia testing in the $1 billion settlement of concussion claims, according to a proposed deal filed Wednesday in federal court.}}</ref>

[[University of Delaware]] professor [[Linda Gottfredson]] has been very critical of this practice,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gottfredson|first1=Linda S.|title=The science and politics of race-norming.|journal=[[American Psychologist]]|date=1994|volume=49|issue=11|pages=955–963|doi=10.1037/0003-066X.49.11.955|pmid=7985887}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gottfredson|first1=Linda S|title=Reconsidering fairness: A matter of social and ethical priorities|journal=[[Journal of Vocational Behavior]]|date=December 1988|volume=33|issue=3|pages=293–319|doi=10.1016/0001-8791(88)90041-3}}</ref> as have conservative columnist [[George Will]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/1991/05/23/seeing-nothing-normal-in-race-norming/ |title=Seeing Nothing Normal in 'Race-Norming' |last=Will |first=George F. |website=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=23 May 1991}}</ref> and law professor [[Robert J. Delahunty]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Delahunty|first1=Robert J|title=Perspectives on within-group scoring|journal=Journal of Vocational Behavior|date=December 1988|volume=33|issue=3|pages=463–477|doi=10.1016/0001-8791(88)90051-6}}</ref> Criticism was based on the perception that race-norming was biased in favor of blacks.<ref>{{Cite book|title=White House Daze: The Unmaming Domestic Policy in the Bush Years|last=Kolb|first=Charles|date=1994|publisher=The Free Press|isbn=0-684-86388-X|location=New York|page=256}}</ref> In the 1980s, the [[Reagan administration]] ordered a study into the unadjusted [[General Aptitude Test Battery]] (without race-norming); the results, released in 1989, showed that unadjusted test scores were not strongly related to job performance.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.newsweek.com/test-cases-how-race-norming-works-204108 |title=Test Cases: How 'Race-Norming' Works |website=[[Newsweek]] |date=2 June 1991}}</ref>

On June 2, 2021, the [[National Football League]] (NFL) announced they would stop using race-norming, as part of their press release for a $1 billion dollar concussion settlement.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-06-02|title=NFL to halt 'race-norming,' review Black claims|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/31554110/nfl-halt-race-norming-review-black-claims-1-billion-concussion-settlement|access-date=2021-06-04|website=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|language=en}}</ref> Race-stratified Heaton, Grant, and Matthews norms, originally published for the [[Halstead–Reitan Neuropsychological Battery]] in 1991 and revised in 2004, had been used in the settlement's claims-evaluation process, contributing to the denial of [[dementia]] claims by Black retired players whose scores would have qualified for benefits had White norms been applied.<ref name="Heaton1991">{{cite book |last1=Heaton |first1=Robert K. |last2=Grant |first2=Igor |last3=Matthews |first3=Charles G. |title=Comprehensive Norms for an Expanded Halstead–Reitan Battery: Demographic Corrections, Research Findings, and Clinical Applications |publisher=Psychological Assessment Resources |date=1991}}</ref><ref name="Heaton2004">{{cite book |last1=Heaton |first1=Robert K. |last2=Miller |first2=S. Walden |last3=Taylor |first3=Michael J. |last4=Grant |first4=Igor |title=Revised Comprehensive Norms for an Expanded Halstead–Reitan Battery: Demographically Adjusted Neuropsychological Norms for African American and Caucasian Adults |publisher=Psychological Assessment Resources |date=2004}}</ref><ref name="Hobson2021"/> The issue had been raised in a 2020 federal lawsuit filed in the [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania|Eastern District of Pennsylvania]] by two former players, Najeh Davenport and Kevin Henry, and was the subject of investigative reporting by ''[[The Washington Post]]'' in August 2021.<ref name="Hobson2021"/> In March 2022, the presiding court approved a modification of the settlement that removed race-based scoring and provided for re-scoring of affected claims.<ref name="DaleAP2022">{{cite news |last=Dale |first=Maryclaire |title=Judge approves fix to stem race bias in NFL concussion deal |agency=Associated Press |via=Sports Illustrated |date=4 March 2022 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2022/03/04/judge-approves-fix-to-stem-race-bias-in-nfl-concussion-deal}}</ref> By August 2022, more than 300 Black retired players who had originally been denied claims had qualified for benefits or league-funded medical treatment under the revised process.<ref name="Hobson2022">{{cite news |last=Hobson |first=Will |title=Hundreds of Black former NFL players get awards after end of 'race-norming' |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=12 August 2022 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/08/12/nfl-race-norming-settlements/}}</ref>

Within [[clinical neuropsychology]], the use of race norming has been debated. In a 2009 review in ''[[Neuropsychology Review]]'', Gasquoine argued that race-stratified norms treat a [[Race (human categorization)|socially defined category]] as if it were biological, and may either mask pathology in patients of one group or exaggerate it in another, depending on the direction of the adjustment.<ref name="Gasquoine2009"/> In November 2021, the Relevance 2050 Subcommittee of the American Academy of Clinical Neuropsychology issued a position statement supporting the elimination of race as a variable in demographically based normative test interpretation.<ref name="AACN2021">{{cite report |author=AACN Relevance 2050 Subcommittee |title=Position Statement on Use of Race as a Factor in Neuropsychological Test Norming and Performance Prediction |publisher=American Academy of Clinical Neuropsychology |date=November 2021 |url=https://theaacn.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/AACN-Position-Statement-on-Race-Norms.pdf}}</ref>
